tn_red_light_district_the.blurb: Near the far left end of the Foster Falls cliffline, this sandstone section is built around a protruding box formation with a big corner between two walls. A short stroll beyond the Snatch Wall brings you to a ledge above the trail where the first several lines begin. Of its 19 routes, 16 are sport and 3 are trad. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.13, with the bulk sitting between 5.9 and 5.10, a few 5.11s and 5.12s, and one 5.13 for the strong. Plenty of moderate bolted climbing makes it a good stop once the easier walls are full.

tn_s_the_red_baron_wall.blurb: One of the longer bolted walls at Woodcock Cove, a roughly mile-long sandstone cliffline above the Sequatchie Valley near Dunlap. All 18 routes here are sport climbs, and none are for beginners: grades start around 5.10, roughly eight of them cluster in the 5.12s, and a few reach into 5.13. Lines run longer than at many of the cove's other walls, and the face looks south, so it collects good sun and suits cooler days. At least one line opens with a bouldery start up an orange lichen streak. A climbers' trail passes the project zone on the way in.

tn_o_the_distillery_aka_still_house_left.blurb: A varied cluster of lines on the sandstone cliffline at Woodcock Cove, near Dunlap in the Sequatchie Valley. Of its 18 routes, 15 are sport and 3 are trad, so you can bring either a quickdraw rack or a trad set. The grades spread widely, from easy 5.6 and 5.7 climbs through a middle group in the 5.8 to 5.9 range, then several 5.11s and 5.12s, with a few 5.13s at the top end. Lines are exposed and the wall faces mostly south. Getting in involves a short scramble down with a rope assist, so allow a little extra time.

tn_toxic_wall.blurb: This short, steeply overhanging limestone band sits beside the Stones River, a little downstream of Percy Priest Dam in Nashville. It is mostly a bouldering spot: 16 problems that run from VB to about V4, with the most common grades at V2 to V4, plus a couple of short sport lines. The rock is sharp but mostly solid, and the climbs are short and powerful rather than tall. Late afternoon is best in summer and sunny winter days are pleasant; otherwise it can be very hot or very cold. Some problems finish near the river's edge, so bring a spotter you trust.

tn_brohemian.blurb: A compact sandstone wall in the Dinner Branch zone near Graysville, a few steps from Bachelor Buttress and nearly part of the same cliff. All 18 routes are bolted. They run from 5.9 up to 5.12, with the large majority split evenly between 5.10 and 5.11 and only a few at 5.12. That makes it a solid pick for climbers working through the low and mid grades of hard sport climbing. The wall stays pleasantly shady in summer, though spiders are common. Getting to the zone means a steep uphill walk with a shallow creek crossing, so it stays fairly quiet.
